subject: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit
messages:
From: Brenda Ortiz <brenda@acmepayments.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Payments Legal <legal@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

Hi Ethan / Ben,

Quick note from the operations team at Acme Payments — we have a planned data-migration maintenance window across our EU clusters on the nights of Apr 25-28 (00:00–06:00 UTC). During that time we expect a spike in automated reconciliation traffic and a small but non-zero risk of P1 incidents tied to our batch processing.

We understand Redwood's standard SLOs, but we need the following: a temporary carveout granting a 4-hour P1 response window overnight (00:00–06:00 UTC) for the four nights above, plus a standby credit as compensation if a P1 is not acknowledged within the requested window. Our security and legal teams asked for an agreed escalation ladder and a formal amendment to the contract.

I attached the filled SLA exception request form and a spreadsheet of expected batch loads. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate this and what the standby credit would look like? Also please include the escalation contacts we should use if an incident is detected on our side.

Thanks,
Brenda Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Payments

Attachments: SLA-Exception-Request-Form.pdf

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Brenda Ortiz <brenda@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

Hi Brenda — thanks for the details and the form. Appreciated — we've reviewed the batch forecast.

Quick summary of our proposal:
- Temporary carveout: April 25 00:00 UTC through April 28 06:00 UTC. During that window Redwood will provide a 4-hour acknowledgment & initial remediation window for incidents classified as P1. P2 remains our standard 8-hour acknowledgement.
- Standby credit: if a P1 is not acknowledged within the 4-hour window, Redwood will issue a standby credit equal to 2x the per-incidence token cost up to a cap of $10,000 per incident (we can make this a flat credit if you prefer).
- Escalation ladder: primary on-call -> senior duty engineer -> on-call manager -> Marissa (CS) for account-level decisions. We'll include direct phone escalation for that ladder in the amendment.

Next steps:
1) I'll propose an internal routing & approval plan and loop in CS + Support to confirm the rota (cc'd Ben).
2) Once we agree internally we'll send a draft contract amendment (DocuSign) and updated runbook.

Would you be available for a 20-minute sync tomorrow to walk the escalation ladder and confirm contact names/numbers?

Best,
Ethan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

Marissa / Ben / Priyom — forwarding Brenda's request from Acme Payments (attached form). High level: four-night maintenance window in EU, they want a 4-hour P1 acknowledgement overnight and standby credit if we miss it. Proposed standby credit as discussed below. We need:

- Support rota coverage: can we staff a duty rotation across April 25-28 that guarantees a 4-hour P1 ack? Priyom, can you confirm whether we can rely on on-call manager escalation and senior duty engineer within that window for EU timezone?
- Escalation ladder + phone numbers: Ben, please confirm who from SE should be on the ladder for immediate triage.
- Financials: what is our recommended standby credit cap here? I suggested up to $10k per incident (or flat $5k), but happy to follow your guidance.

I put together a draft escalation ladder in the body below for quick review. We need internal approval by EOD Apr 14 to meet Acme's DocuSign timeline.

Draft escalation ladder (internal):
1) On-call responder (first ack) — 4-hour ack target
2) Senior duty engineer (if not acked in 2 hours after page)
3) On-call manager (if unresolved 3 hours after page)
4) CS lead (Marissa) for account-level decisions and standby credit approval

Please reply with edits/approvals; Priyom, if this is feasible say “+1”; if not, propose an alternate.

Thanks,
Ethan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

+1 on feasibility with a small operational caveat. We can staff the 4-hour P1 acknowledgement for those four nights provided we run a pre-approved rotation and define an explicit handover checklist. Priyom — please make sure the rotation is covered by two separate people per night (primary + secondary) and include contact numbers.

Minor edits to the ladder:
- Make "Senior duty engineer" the secondary page after 90 minutes rather than 2 hours (so we have an earlier escalation).
- Add an automatic status update at T+2 hours to Acme's incident channel with initial triage notes.

I'll attach the Support-Rotation-Calendar.xlsx with a suggested schedule and numbers. If legal wants a reduced monetary cap we can move to a flat-rate credit of $6,000 per missed ack — that simplifies billing and approvals.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Support-Rotation-Calendar.xlsx

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Brenda Ortiz <brenda@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

Hi Brenda — following our internal review here’s the agreed plan we can put in a short-term amendment:

1) Coverage window: Apr 25 00:00 UTC — Apr 28 06:00 UTC (EU region).
2) P1 acknowledgement: 4-hour target overnight; P2 unchanged at 8 hours.
3) Escalation ladder (final):
   - On-call responder (T0) — initial page/ack target 4 hours
   - Senior duty engineer (T+90m) — escalation if no meaningful progress
   - On-call manager (T+3h) — account-level decisions and payment/credit authority
   - Marissa Cole, VP CS (direct escalate if account-level is needed)
4) Standby credit: flat $6,000 credit per missed P1 acknowledgement (this replaces the earlier per-incident cap suggestion to simplify). Credit will be applied to the next invoice; maximum two credits across the 4-night window.
5) Runbook & rota: we will attach the runbook and a rotation calendar (see attachment).

I've also created a short draft amendment (Draft-Amendment.docx) and a DocuSign link to sign once you confirm the contact phone numbers we should use. Link: https://docusign.example/sign/AMCP-2027-044

If you confirm we’ll send the DocuSign and the runbook. Are the credit terms and ladder acceptable?

Best,
Ethan

From: Brenda Ortiz <brenda@acmepayments.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Payments Legal <legal@acmepayments.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight P1/P2 SLA carveout + standby credit

Ethan — thanks, that looks good. We accept the $6,000 flat standby credit (cap of two credits across the maintenance window) and the escalation ladder as written.

Confirming the two primary escalation contacts:
- Brenda Ortiz (platform ops) — +44 20 7946 0931
- Jamal Harris (on-call infra) — +44 7712 345678

Please send the DocuSign and runbook. Legal will review the amendment this afternoon.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Brenda
Head of Platform Operations | Acme Payments
